config.title: Test Error Boundary

intro.title: Test Error Boundary
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a test for an Error Boundary component in React using TypeScript. You will learn how to simulate errors in a child component to verify that your Error Boundary correctly catches them and displays a fallback UI. The core concept involves using React's Error Boundary lifecycle and Jest testing utilities to ensure your application handles runtime errors gracefully. You will work with React, TypeScript, Jest, and React Testing Library to create and run a test that validates the error-handling behavior. This practice helps you write more robust applications by testing error scenarios effectively.
intro.usecase: Error boundaries are essential in production React applications to prevent entire dashboards or complex interfaces from crashing due to isolated component failures. In financial dashboards displaying live charts and data feeds, a single faulty widget shouldn't bring down the entire trading interface. E-commerce product pages use error boundaries to ensure that if a recommendation carousel fails, users can still add items to cart and complete purchases. This pattern allows developers to gracefully degrade specific UI sections while maintaining core application functionality.

objectives: Implement a React Error Boundary component using TypeScript
Configure the Error Boundary to catch and handle runtime errors in child components
Initialize fallback UI states to display when errors occur
Integrate the Error Boundary component into an existing React application structure
Manipulate component state to control error display and recovery behavior
Render error information and user-friendly messages in the fallback UI
Apply the Error Boundary to wrap specific components for targeted error handling

steps.title: Import React and createErrorBoundary from @sentry/react
steps.instruction: Import React and the createErrorBoundary function from @sentry/react.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with curly braces for named exports.
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary imports for error boundary testing are added.
successCriteria: React is imported from 'react' and createErrorBoundary is imported from '@sentry/react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both React from 'react' and createErrorBoundary from '@sentry/react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are not correct. You need to import React from 'react' and createErrorBoundary from '@sentry/react'.

steps.title: Create a component that throws an error
steps.instruction: Define a functional component named ErrorComponent that throws an error when rendered.
steps.hint: Create a component that throws an Error inside its render logic. You can use either function declaration or arrow function syntax.
steps.expectedOutcome: A component named ErrorComponent that throws an error when rendered.
successCriteria: ErrorComponent is defined and throws an error.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a component, but it might not throw an error yet. Make sure it throws an Error when rendered.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly or doesn't throw an error. Check the component name and error throwing logic.

steps.title: Create the ErrorBoundary component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named ErrorBoundary using the imported createErrorBoundary function. Return the result of calling createErrorBoundary with a fallback UI function that returns a simple error message.
steps.hint: Call createErrorBoundary with a function that returns JSX. The fallback function should accept props and return something like a paragraph with an error message.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new ErrorBoundary component is defined using createErrorBoundary with a fallback UI.
successCriteria: ErrorBoundary component is created with createErrorBoundary and a fallback function returning JSX.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using createErrorBoundary and returning a component with a fallback function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ErrorBoundary component wasn't created correctly. Review how to use createErrorBoundary with a fallback UI.

steps.title: Add error state to ErrorBoundary
steps.instruction: Inside the ErrorBoundary component, import useState from 'react' and declare const [error, setError] = useState<Error | null>(null).
steps.hint: You'll need to import useState from 'react' and declare a state variable like const [error, setError] = useState<Error | null>(null).
steps.expectedOutcome: The ErrorBoundary component will have an error state variable initialized to null.
successCriteria: useState is imported from 'react' and an error state variable is declared with type Error | null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've imported useState from 'react' and declared the error state with the correct type.
steps.feedbackWrong: The error state wasn't added correctly. Check that you imported useState and declared const [error, setError] = useState<Error | null>(null).

steps.title: Implement componentDidCatch lifecycle method
steps.instruction: Inside your ErrorBoundary component, implement the componentDidCatch lifecycle method. The method should take two parameters: error and errorInfo. Inside the method, call setError to update the error state with the error parameter.
steps.hint: Add a componentDidCatch method inside the ErrorBoundary component. Use the error parameter to update the state.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ErrorBoundary component now has a componentDidCatch method that updates the error state when an error occurs.
successCriteria: The ErrorBoundary component contains a componentDidCatch method that calls setError with the error parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added componentDidCatch, but make sure it properly updates the error state using setError with the error parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: The componentDidCatch method is missing or doesn't update the error state correctly. Check that you're calling setError with the error parameter inside componentDidCatch.

steps.title: Add retry functionality to fallback
steps.instruction: In the ErrorFallback component, add a function named handleRetry that resets the error state by calling the resetErrorBoundary function passed as a prop.
steps.hint: Create a function inside ErrorFallback that calls the resetErrorBoundary prop when invoked.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ErrorFallback component will have a handleRetry function that can be used to reset the error boundary when the retry button is clicked.
successCriteria: ErrorFallback contains a handleRetry function that calls the resetErrorBoundary prop.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the retry handler function.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a function, but make sure it's named handleRetry and calls resetErrorBoundary().
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleRetry function is missing or doesn't properly call resetErrorBoundary.

steps.title: Create main App component with error boundary
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that wraps the ErrorComponent with the ErrorBoundary component.
steps.hint: Define a new component that returns the ErrorBoundary with ErrorComponent as its child.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is defined and returns the ErrorBoundary wrapping ErrorComponent.
successCriteria: App component exists and returns ErrorBoundary with ErrorComponent as its child.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a component, but make sure it's named App and wraps ErrorComponent inside ErrorBoundary.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component is not correctly defined or doesn't wrap ErrorComponent with ErrorBoundary.

steps.title: Add trigger button to simulate errors
steps.instruction: In the App component, add a button that conditionally renders the ErrorComponent when clicked to trigger errors.
steps.hint: You'll need to add state to track whether to show the error component, and update that state when the button is clicked.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component should include a button that, when clicked, shows the ErrorComponent to trigger an error that will be caught by the ErrorBoundary.
successCriteria: App component has useState hook for showError state
Button with onClick handler toggles showError state
Conditional rendering shows ErrorComponent when showError is true
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have: 1) useState for showError state, 2) button with onClick handler, and 3) conditional rendering of ErrorComponent.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component doesn't yet have a working trigger button. Review the example and try again.

steps.title: Test the error boundary implementation
steps.instruction: In the App component, add a button that triggers the error by setting state to cause the ErrorComponent to render.
steps.hint: Add a button with an onClick handler that updates state to conditionally render the ErrorComponent.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will have a button that, when clicked, triggers the error boundary to catch and display the error.
successCriteria: App component includes a button with onClick handler that conditionally renders ErrorComponent.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you have both the button and the conditional rendering logic for ErrorComponent.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you added a button with an onClick handler and the conditional rendering for ErrorComponent.
